item.name: Create paginated transaction queries for all LOBs summary data based on search criteria

request.name: Create paginated transaction queries for all LOBs summary data based on search criteria

description.content:
This API call allows the client to submit a request for retrieving transactions for a specified search criteria (All LOB summary).

Request Specifications:

Attribute
Required/optional
Type
Description
start_date, end_date Required String Specific date range for which the transaction data is requested.The date range to fetch the booking transactions data. Timestamp in format: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS. (Example: 2020-05-05 09:00:00) These should come as a pair.Note: Future date is only allowed if the date_type is set as travel_date.
  • Both start and end date is mandatory. If either start date or end date is missing it will it throw an error
  • Default timezone is UTC
locale Optional String Locale represents the supported language to get the report. Accepted values are: nb-NO, de-DE, en-US, en-CA, es-ES, fr-CA, it-IT, nl-NL, sv-SE, en-AU, da-DK, fr-FR, en-GB (Defult locale is en-US) Note: This value is case sensitive.
currency_code Optional String 3 character currency code to get the amount in given currency. Accepted Values are: CHF, ARS, MXN, CLP, ZAR, INR, VND, CNY, THB, AUD, ILS, JPY, PLN, GBP, IDR, PHP, TRY, RUB, AED, HKD, EUR, COP, DKK, CAD, MYR, USD, NOK, SGD, CZK, SEK, NZD, BRL, UAH
includes Optional String To include custom data fields in the response. Custom data fields will now come in response only when requested by users in the include option. Values: ["cdf"]
report_level Optional String Report level for the LOB's air and train to retrieve data for a specific report level. "ticket, segment, leg" are the three different requests configured by report_level field. If this data is not provided Ticket Level data will be returned by default
date_type Optional String The date type to search the records. You can search for records based on travel date as well as issue date. "Issue date" and "travel date" will provide data based on issue date and travel date respectively. If no value is passed as datetype, issue date will be considered by default. Accepted Values are: issue_date,travel_date Note : Issue date cannot be future date. However, travel date can be a future date or past date.
active_records_only Optional String A string to select only the records with active ticket status or all records, present for a given start and end date. The possible values for the string are "true" or "false". By default, it is set as false which would show all the records for a time period. By passing true, you can exclude bookings and items that have been cancelled, exchanged, voided, or refunded.
client_ids Optional List With this parameter, it becomes possible for a client or a partner to specify the companies for which they want the reporting data. It accepts a list of the client ids given in string format. If no value is given, by default data will be returned for all associated companies for the client. Note: Passing incorrect company Id values or non numeric values would return an error.
reconciled_records_only Optional String A string to select only the reconciled records, present for a given start and end date. The possible values for the string are "true" or "false". By default, it is set as false which would show all the records for a time period. By passing true, you recieve only the records undergoing reconciliation process.
Example:

  POST https://apis.egencia.com/bi/api/v1/transactions
    {
       "start_date": "2018-01-01 09:00:00",
       "end_date": "2018-05-05 09:00:00",
       "locale": "en-US",
       "currency_code": "USD",
       "date_type": "issue_date",
       "active_records_only":"true",
       "client_ids":["10098","13882","19120"],
       "reconciled_records_only":"true"
    }
     -> 201 CREATED
    {
     "metadata": {
       "page_limit": 5000,
       "total_records": 10000,
       "total_pages": 2,
       "latest_reconciled_date": "2018-04-29 00:00:00"
     },
     "_links": {
       "first": {
         "href": "https://apis.egencia.com/bi/api/v1/transactions/3004fa51-104e-4712-b34d-bf7635eb2958?page=1"
       },
       "last": {
         "href": "https://apis.egencia.com/bi/api/v1/transactions/3004fa51-104e-4712-b34d-bf7635eb2958?page=2"
       }
     },
     "report_id": "3004fa51-104e-4712-b34d-bf7635eb2958"
   }

This API will return the metadata (hyperlinks) of the resource from where all the qualified transactions will be fetched in a paginated manner.

Public BI Transactions API is a generic and secure solution to allow clients to access their previous booking transaction data dynamically for different dates and other user query filters such as ob, locale, currency code or report level.

Base Endpoint URL

The Endpoint URL for communicating with the Transaction API system is:

POST {{transactionUrl}}

Please note the use of the https protocol. This ensures that all data that travels between the server and your program are encrypted. This protects your credentials and the transmitted data.

Authentication

Before you can access the BI Transactions API, you need to authenticate and authorise who you are. Our API uses the OAuth 2.0 standard for authentication.

Note: All API requests must be made over HTTPS. Calls made over plain HTTP will fail. API requests without authentication will also fail.

Before calling Transaction data API the client should be successfully authorized with Egencia's Authentication service. The access token generated within authorization step should be provided in the further call(s) to the API.

Authorization

Egencia transaction data API supports access token based on OAuth2.0 protocol. A client ID and Client Secret ID will be generated and shared to the client.

Client IDs and Secrets

The Client ID and Client Secret are like a username and password that authenticate your application. They aren't used directly in making most API requests, instead, they are exchanged for tokens, which are used to make the actual requests.

All requests to the OAuth 2.0 endpoint must be given your credentials in the form of Basic authentication. To comply with the HTTP requirements, your Client ID and Secret should be encoded in base 64.

Make sure to keep the client secret secure - anyone who has it can impersonate your application!

Endpoint
Headers
HTTP method
Endpoint
Headers
HTTP method
/auth/v1/tokens Authorization: Basic base64encode(client_id:client_secret)
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded 		Post

Post the client_id and client_secret to the URL {{authUrl}} to obtain an access token which you can then use to call BI Transactions APIs. 

Examples

Request

{ "client_id":"lliz84o5554csgss8s48gss", "grant_type":"client_credentials" }

Response (status code = 200)

{ "access_token": "JWT access token", "expires_in": 3600, "token_type": "Bearer" }

The access token generated within Authorization call kept alive within expiration time provided in the successful authorization response, no need to generate new access token each time the Client calls BI Reporting API until it expires. Expiration time provided in seconds.

NOTE:

  • The values for client id and client secret will be provided to the Client after on-boarding to Egencia API platform.
  • All the fields provided in the request-response samples are mandatory.

Overview Of BI Transactions API

The Egencia BI Transactions API is the new solution that is being offered to clients for accessing their booking data in a programmatic method. With the help of the Egencia BI Transactions API you can

  • Retrieve data for your custom reports programmatically in JSON format
  • Apply filters as request parameters and automate reporting tasks

Pagination

Doing a POST of BI API will return the metadata (hyperlinks) of the resource from where all the qualified transactions will be fetched in a paginated manner. You can page through the resource by making a GET request to the "next" URL provided in the paginated response. If there are no more pages, "next" will be set null. The users can page through any valid page number at any time using the Get request.

Introduction to IATA Code API

IATA Code API offers an interface for customers and partners to retrieve IATA codes for the specified Point of Sale or all Point of Sales in case none specified from Egencia. This API is organised around REST /JSON over HTTPS for data retrieval. The API returns JSON responses and uses standard HTTPs response codes, authentication, and verbs.

Versioning

Note: Please refer to the Versioning section of the BI Transaction API for further information regarding versioning

Implementation method

This public API solution allows clients to access the IATA codes based on the Point of Sales for different transactions obtained from the Transaction API response.

Endpoint

/v1/egencia_iata
Method GET
Content-type  application/json
Accept application/json

Base Endpoint URL

The Endpoint URL for communicating with the IATA Code API system is:

GET {{posIataUrl}}

Please note the use of the https protocol. This ensures that all data that travels between the server and your program are encrypted. This protects your credentials and the transmitted data.

Authentication

Authentication for the IATA Code API is same as that of the Transactions API where the API supports access token based on OAuth2.0 protocol. You can use the same client ID and Client Secret ID as BI API for calling IATA Code API

Note: Please refer to the Authentication section of the BI Transaction API for further information

Request & Response

Method Endpoint Description
GET /v1/egencia_iata?pos={point_of_sale} Gets IATA code based on the POS

Request Parameters

Attribute Required/Optional Type Description
pos Optional String Point of Sale for which the user wants to get the IATA code. If absent, gets all the available IATA Codes

Response Parameters

Attribute Type Description
pos String Point of Sale
iata String IATA code for the specified Point of sale
